text:
Johan (Client): hey team, we started getting 429s every night around 01:15 during our end-of-day sync. started small then within ~90s we see thousands of calls get 429. impact: failed invoice exports. can you help?
Alex (Support): sorry to hear that. can you share a sample x-request-id and the region where this is hitting? also your plan (free/prod/dedicated)?
Johan (Client): thanks. hitting hosted-us-west. plan=standard-prod. sample header from one failed request: 
```
x-request-id: 01H7X2-abc123
x-forwarded-for: 52.24.12.8
x-client-concurrency: 16
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
```
we run a worker that parallelizes 30 files -> each file spawns 10 parallel streams so big fanout.
Alex (Support): ok. can you confirm the cadence? cron at 01:15:00 exact? any retries/backoff configured?
Johan (Client): yes cron fires at 01:15 exactly. retries: naive immediate 3x with small fixed delays (1s, 1s, 1s). no jitter.
Priya (SRE): looking at edge traces for tenant 9876: lots of simultaneous connections at 01:15:11-01:15:40. rate limiter logs show per-minute window exhaustion: tokens consumed in first 18s of minute. excerpt from logs: 
```
[01:15:12] tenant=9876 allow=FALSE reason=RPM_LIMIT_EXCEEDED remaining=0 window_start=01:15:00
[01:15:13] tenant=9876 requests=3190 burst=1200
```
This is classic minute-boundary stampede + high concurrency. HTTP/2 multiplexing means many logical streams push through one TCP connection so our per-connection smoothing didn't help.
Ingrid (Eng Runtime): we can mitigate a few ways: short-term: recommend client-side jitter + reduce max parallel streams per worker to 4-6 and implement exponential backoff with randomized jitter. medium: enable per-tenant smoothing (leaky bucket) on the edge to spread tokens across the minute instead of letting full burst consume it on second 1. long-term: add a configurable per-second refill or allow reserved burst for scheduled jobs (but that's product/quotas change).
Alex (Support): suggested immediate guidance to customer: 1) stagger cron start by random 0-60s jitter 2) cap concurrency (x-client-concurrency) to 4 3) switch retries to exp backoff with jitter (e.g., retry_after = 2^n + rand(0,3)) 4) if they need sustained high throughput, submit quota bump request.
Johan (Client): can we get a short-lived quota bump while we refactor the worker? export jobs need ~1200rpm for 3 mins only.
Priya (SRE): short-lived bump possible but needs ops approval. I'll open SUP-7891 and propose a 2-hour elevated window for tonight so they can drain backlog. note: bump will not fix the root cause (minute folding) but will reduce immediate failures.
Ingrid (Eng Runtime): I'll sketch a runtime change to add optional per-second smoothing with a small token reservoir for scheduled jobs. could be behind feature flag. ETA for prototype ~2 weeks.
Alex (Support): action items: - Johan: apply jitter + reduce concurrency tonight (we'll provide example) - Priya: open SUP-7891 and request 2hr bump for tenant 9876 - Ingrid: prototype smoothing feature and advise config options
Johan (Client): thanks. example patch we can apply quickly: 
```
# worker startup delay (bash)
sleep $((RANDOM % 45))
# client concurrency env
export MAX_STREAMS=5
# simple retry pseudo
retry_delay=$((2**$attempt + (RANDOM % 4)))
```
Alex (Support): perfect. once you make changes, attach a short runbook with before/after metrics (requests/min, 429 count). we'll monitor.
DevOpsBot: ticket SUP-7891 created and assigned to SRE (Priya). ETA for ops review: 30m. :white_check_mark:
Priya (SRE): monitoring note: enabling anomaly alert on 429 rate for tenant 9876 and setting temporary alert threshold at 10% of requests returning 429 for next 6 hours.
Alex (Support): I'll follow up with the customer at 01:40 to confirm if bump + jitter cleared it. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
